title: A Generalized Model for Disordered Random Sequential Adsorption with Charge-Dependent Deposition
authors: G. Palacios, A. M. S. Macêdo
abstract: We generalize a one-dimensional random sequential adsorption model (RSA) of charged unit segments in which the deposition position follows a beta kernel determined by the charges bounding the available gap and those of the incoming particle. The interaction parameter \(0\leqλ<1\) interpolates between uniform car parking and strongly localized deposition. We derive a four component generating function equation that provides exact recursions for the complete occupation statistics, although only the mean and variance are analyzed in detail here. Exact finite-shell solutions serve as benchmarks for the Gauss--Jacobi quadrature and Monte Carlo simulations. We prove that, although boundary charges affect finite size behavior, the four boundary states have the same asymptotic mean and variance densities, consequently, we prove that the jammed density is self-averaging. Numerical results show that charge selectivity increases the coverage, especially for mixtures dominated by opposite endpoint charges, which also exhibit strongly reduced fluctuations near \(λ=1\). The model provides a tractable connection between uniform RSA, dynamically generated disorder, and interaction-driven deposition.
summary: This work develops a generalized 1D Random Sequential Adsorption model where particle deposition is biased by electrostatic interactions between charges. By deriving exact statistical recursions and performing asymptotic analysis, the authors show that charge selectivity enhances packing density and reduces statistical fluctuations compared to uniform deposition. This provides a powerful, tractable framework connecting simple geometric processes to complex, interaction-driven disorder.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the 1D Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) model to account for charge-dependent deposition probabilities, linking uniform deposition to interaction-driven processes.
main_result: Charge selectivity significantly increases the packing density, especially when opposite charges dominate the deposition, and the jammed density is proven to be self-averaging.
method: The authors derive exact recursion relations using a four-component probability-generating-function equation and validate results using Gauss–Jacobi quadrature and Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D line where charged segments adsorb sequentially. The deposition probability is governed by a Beta kernel dependent on the charges bounding the available gap and the incoming particle's charges.
key_observables: Mean and variance of the occupation statistics ($ho$ and $\chi$), and the jammed density.
important_parameters: The interaction parameter $\lambda$ ($0 \le \lambda < 1$), which controls the strength of charge-dependent interactions, and the particle composition ($p$).
main_assumptions: The model assumes that the deposition probability is prescribed by the boundary charges, allowing for a continuous interpolation between uniform RSA and strongly localized deposition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the charge-dependent deposition kernel for various charge configurations and show the asymptotic mean and variance densities ($ho$ and $\chi$) as a function of $\lambda$ and particle composition.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the generalized RSA model via a Beta kernel, deriving the exact recursive equations for statistics, and finally performing asymptotic analysis comparing Monte Carlo and quadrature results to quantify the effect of charge selectivity.
why_interesting: While focused on classical adsorption, the concept of using interaction-dependent kernels to model deposition/fragmentation processes is mathematically analogous to modeling energy landscapes or interaction-driven state transitions in quantum many-body systems.
